From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Not to be confused with [Aria the Scarlet Ammo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aria_the_Scarlet_Ammo).

**Aria** (stylized as **ARIA**) is a Japanese [manga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manga) series written and illustrated by [Kozue Amano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kozue_Amano). The series was originally titled **Aqua** (stylized as **AQUA**) when it was published in [Enix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enix)'s Monthly Stencil magazine in 2001, and retitled when it was transferred to [Mag Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mag_Garden)'s [Comic Blade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_Blade), where it continued serialization from 2002 to 2008. Aqua was collected in two [tankōbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tank%C5%8Dbon) volumes, and Aria was collected in twelve volumes.

[Hal Film Maker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hal_Film_Maker) has adapted the manga into several [anime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anime) television series. A first season was broadcast in 2005, a second season in 2006, an [OVA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Original_video_animation) released September 2007, and a third season in 2008 that ended around the same time as the manga serialization. An OVA, titled Aria the Avvenire, was released in the anime series' 10th anniversary Blu-ray box sets between December 2015 and June 2016. A film to celebrate the 15th anniversary of the anime series titled Aria the Crepuscolo premiered on 5 March 2021. A second anime film titled Aria the Benedizione premiered on 3 December 2021.

[ADV Manga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.D._Vision) released English translations of the first three volumes of Aria in 2004 before dropping the license. [Tokyopop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyopop) then acquired the English-language rights to Aqua as well as Aria. Tokyopop released the two volumes of Aqua in October 2007 and February 2008 and six volumes of Aria between January 2008 and December 2010. The anime is licensed in North America by [The Right Stuf International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Right_Stuf_International), which released all three seasons in box sets under its Nozomi Entertainment imprint between 30 September 2008 and 2 March 2010.
The series is set in the 24th century on a [terraformed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terraformed) Mars, now named Aqua, and follows a young woman named Akari

Aria Company [\[ edit \]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aria_%28manga%29&action=edit&section=3)
Aria Company is a small water-guide company that starts with only two employees. Its uniforms are lined with blue, and its president (and namesake) is Aria Pokoteng.
Akari Mizunashi (水無灯里, Mizunashi Akari)
Voiced by: [Erino Hazuki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erino_Hazuki)<sup>[11]</sup>(Japanese); [Veronica Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronica_Taylor)<sup>[12]</sup> ( ng s ) E li h

A native of Japan on Manhome (Earth) who immigrates to Aqua when she is 15 to become an Undine. While not as skillful at rowing a gondola as Alice nor as familiar with the history of her adopted city as Aika, Akari makes friends quickly and easily converses with customers and other strangers. She is depicted as optimistic and cheerful,<sup>[1]</sup> finding enjoyment in things or events that others think are humdrum and mundane,<sup>[13]</sup> for which Aika and Alice call her "mysterious"; in the anime, Aika and Alice separately comment that Akari seems to attract mysterious phenomena to her. Akari often says Hohe or Hahi, which is her short version of "wow". When Akari used gondola simulations on Manhome, she accidentally learned how to row backwards and has to relearn the proper method when she starts at Aria Company; however, as Alicia puts it, "When rowing backward, Akari-chan is unrivaled!"<sup>[14]</sup> Most chapters of the manga and episodes of the anime are [framed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Framing_device) with [narration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narrator) taken from e-mails written by Akari. In the anime, the recipient is a young girl named Ai, a customer in the first episode who becomes Akari's [pen pal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pen_pal),<sup>[15]</sup> but in the manga the recipient is someone she does not name and is referred to as zenryaku but has never seen.

At the start of Aqua, Akari arrives on Aqua as a new Pair (apprentice) at Aria Company. In chapter 5 of Aqua, when Aika is promoted to Single (journeyman), Alicia tests and promotes Akari as well. Later, in chapter 58 of Aria and episode 12 of Aria the Origination, after Aika is promoted to Prima (full Undine), Alicia gives Akari the test for Prima.

For a long time, Alice was not confident in her singing skills until Athena advised her to enjoy what she sings and not worry about her performance. In volume 11 of Aria, after Alice graduates from middle school, she is promoted to Prima straight from Pair, the first Undine to do so, and is given the title "Orange Princess" (黄昏の姫君, Tasogare no Himegimi; lit. "Twilight Princess").
Athena Glory (アテナ・グローリィ, Atena Gurōryi)

Voiced by: [Tomoko Kawakami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomoko_Kawakami),<sup>[11]</sup> [Rina Satō](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rina_Sat%C5%8D) (2021 film)<sup>[41]</sup>(Japanese); [Michele Knotz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michele_Knotz)<sup>[16]</sup> (English) One of Neo-Venezia's Three Water Fairies, known by the title "[Siren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siren_%28mythology%29)" (天上の謳声, Tenjō no Utagoe; lit. "Heavenly Voice") for her beautiful singing voice. She is Alice's mentor at Orange Planet. She is quiet most of the time and often appears to be an [airhead](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/airhead) who does not pay attention to her surroundings (in the anime, she is shown more than once forgetting to duck while rowing under a bridge), but she genuinely cares about Alice. Athena has a strange laugh that comes out sounding as though she is angry. She was a trainee Undine with Alicia and Akira. She joined them in joint practice sessions like Akari, Aika, and Alice do now. At the conclusion of the series, Athena semi-retires from being an Undine to debut as an [opera singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opera_singer).
**Atora Monteverdi** (アトーラ・モンテヴェルディ, Atōra Monteverudi)
Voiced by: [Houko Kuwashima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houko_Kuwashima)<sup>[42]</sup>(Japanese); [Debora Rabbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debora_Rabbai)<sup>[35]</sup> (English)

Atora is a Single for Orange Planet who appears in the Origination series. She often works as a traghetto rower with Anzu as well as Ayumi from Himeya Company. Atora took the Prima exam once but did not pass and became too discouraged to try again. After meeting Akari during her stint in the traghetto, she decides to train harder to retake the exam.
**Anzu Yumeno** (夢野杏, Yumeno Anzu)
Voiced by: [Kana Asumi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kana_Asumi)<sup>[35]</sup>(Japanese); Michaela Bryce<sup>[35]</sup> (English)

Anzu is a Single for Orange Planet who appears in Origination. She often works as a traghetto rower with Atora as well as Ayumi from Himeya Company. Although Anzu has failed her Prima exam several times, she continues to work hard and is determined to become a Prima.

Voiced by: [Ai Kayano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ai_Kayano)<sup>[43]</sup>(Japanese); Erica Schroeder<sup>[44]</sup> (English)
A newly trained Single under Alice in the Avvenire series and the Crepuscolo movie.
**Cats** [\[ edit \]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aria_%28manga%29&action=edit&section=6)

Because blue-eyed cats are considered lucky on Aqua, all Undine companies have a blue-eyed cat as a mascot, who is given the title President.<sup>[45]</sup> Cats on Aqua have been bred to be as intelligent as humans, though they cannot speak.<sup>[46]</sup>
**President Aria Pokoteng** (アリア・ポコテン, Aria Pokoten)
Voiced by: [Chinami Nishimura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinami_Nishimura_%28voice_actress%29)<sup>[11]</sup>(Japanese); Tara Tisch<sup>[21]</sup> (English)

President and namesake of Aria Company, and an Aqua cat. Aria is large and fat, massing 10 kg.<sup>[47]</sup> He is attracted to President Hime, who does not appear to reciprocate his sentiments; his pursuit of her is a common [comic relief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_relief) scene.
**President Hime M. Granzchesta** (ヒメ・M・グランチェスタ, Hime Emu Guranchesuta)

Voiced by: [Motomu Kiyokawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motomu_Kiyokawa)<sup>[58][59]</sup>(Japanese); [Mike Pollock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pollock_%28voice_actor%29)<sup>[21]</sup> (English)

An elderly mailman in Neo-Venezia, called Mailman-san or Mr. Postman by Akari. He is the first person that Akari meets after arriving on Aqua. He is a kind man who is devoted to his work and his younger co workers. Akari does not learn his name until near the end of the series when he hires her for a gondola ride after retiring from his job.
Terms [\[ edit \]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aria_%28manga%29&action=edit&section=8)
Several terms of the world of Aqua are derived from [elemental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elemental) mythology:<sup>[63]</sup>
[Undine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undine) (水先案内人, Undīne)ウ ン デ ィ ー ネ

A [gondolier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gondolier) acting as a refined tour guide for visitors to Neo-Venezia. All known Undines are young girls and women, except those of the gender-flip parallel world in the Special Navigation of volume 6.
Pair (ペア, Pea)

An apprentice Undine who has just begun practicing [sculling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sculling) a gondola. A Pair is recognized by her pair of gloves, worn to protect her hands as she builds up [calluses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callus). When a Pair is promoted to Single, she removes one glove.<sup>[64]</sup> This is translated by Nozomi and ADV as "Pair", and by Tokyopop as "apprentice".
Single (シングル, Shinguru)

A [journeyman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Journeyman) Undine qualified to take customers only under supervision. So-called because she wears only one glove.<sup>[64]</sup> Nozomi and ADV translate this as "Single," and by Tokyopop as "journeyman."
Prima (プリマ, Purima)

A graduated Undine who is no longer a Single. Once an Undine becomes a Prima, they can take customers without supervision. This is translated by Nozomi and ADV as "Prima", and by Tokyopop as "full-fledged Undine".<sup>[65]</sup>
[Salamander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salamanders_in_folklore_and_legend) (火炎之番人, Saramandā)

A person working at controlling the weather and adding heat to the atmosphere as part of [terraforming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terraforming) Aqua. Salamanders live in floating islands tethered at high altitude.
[Gnome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gnome) (地重管理人, Nōmu)
A person working underground to regulate the gravity of Aqua, so that it is as strong as Manhome (Earth). Because of their environment, most gnomes are short and have bad eyesight.<sup>[62]</sup>
[Sylph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylph) (風追配達人, Shirufu)
A person who makes deliveries by air bike. Deliveries are done by air in Neo-Venezia because only unpowered watercraft such as gondolas are allowed in the smaller canals of the city.<sup>[66]</sup>
[Traghetto](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/traghetto)

A gondola designed to ferry several people across the [Grand Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Canal_%28Venice%29). Because of its size and the number of passengers, the gondola is rowed by two Singles.
Three Water Fairies (水の三大妖精, Mizu no Sandaiyōsei)
Neo-Venezia's three most accomplished Undines at the time of the series: Alicia Florence, Akira E. Ferrari, and Athena Glory.<sup>[32]</sup>

According to Jun'ichi Satō, it was a struggle to fit the available material into the 13 episodes of the first season, which focused closely on Akari.<sup>[79]</sup> The title of the second season, Aria the Natural, came about because he had 26 episodes to work with, letting him treat the story in a more "natural" manner,<sup>[80]</sup> allowing the series to develop other characters more.<sup>[81]</sup>

Choro Club and [Takeshi Senoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takeshi_Senoo) composed 30 works of music for the first season of the anime and 15 for the second.<sup>[82]</sup> Jun'ichi Satō and sound designer Yasuno Satō assigned Choro Club and [Takeshi Senoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takeshi_Senoo) abstract themes instead of plot points,<sup>[83][84]</sup> which was an unfamiliar method for the composers who did not have much experience working for anime shows. [Takeshi Senoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takeshi_Senoo) and the three members of Choro Club make a [cameo appearance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameo_appearance) as musicians in episode 23 of Aria the Natural.<sup>[85]</sup> Jun'ichi Satō has commented that the lyrics for the songs "Barracole" and "Coccolo", sung by [Eri Kawai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eri_Kawai) as the voice of Athena Glory, were gibberish. The lyrics for the first two seasons' theme songs were also initially meant to be gibberish,<sup>[86]</sup> but after reading the manga Eri Kawai decided to write Japanese lyrics: "I read the original manga and wrote the lyrics, using my image of Neo-Venezia as a starting point. Then did my best to match words that flowed with the melody."<sup>[87]</sup> Kawai made demo recordings for [Yui Makino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yui_Makino) as a guide for her performance of the theme songs.<sup>[88]</sup> [Takeshi Senoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takeshi_Senoo) has described "Smile Again", the second ending theme song of Aria the Natural, as a song about the end of summer, and envisioned it being sung by Erino Hazuki as Akari.<sup>[89]</sup>
Media [\[ edit \]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aria_%28manga%29&action=edit&section=11)
Manga [\[ edit \]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aria_%28manga%29&action=edit&section=12)
Main article: [List of Aria chapters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Aria_chapters)

The manga was written and illustrated by [Kozue Amano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kozue_Amano) and has a complicated publishing history. Aqua was originally published by [Enix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enix) in Monthly Stencil magazine from January to September 2001 and collected in two [tankōbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tank%C5%8Dbon) volumes. When the series moved to [Mag Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mag_Garden)'s [Comic Blade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_Blade) magazine in February 2002, the title changed to Aria. Mag Garden later re-released the two volumes of Aqua with additional material and new covers.<sup>[90]</sup> Serialization completed in February 2008. In all, the 70 serialized chapters of Aqua and Aria were collected in 14 [tankōbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tank%C5%8Dbon) volumes, each volume containing five chapters covering a season of the year. Each volume is called a "voyage," and each chapter a "navigation."

In English, Aria (but not Aqua) was originally licensed by ADV Manga, who dropped the license after publishing three volumes.<sup>[6]</sup> The North American license for Aqua and Aria was picked up by [Tokyopop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyopop),<sup>[91][92]</sup> which began releasing the series starting with the first volume of Aqua.<sup>[93]</sup> The series has been licensed in France by Kami,<sup>[94][95]</sup> in Germany by [Tokyopop Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyopop),<sup>[96][97]</sup> in Italy by [Star Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Comics_%28Italy%29),<sup>[98][99]</sup> in Indonesia by [M&C Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M&C_Comics),<sup>[100][101]</sup> in South Korea by Bookbox,<sup>[102]</sup> in Spain by [Editorial Ivrea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Editorial_Ivrea),<sup>[103]</sup> in Taiwan by [Tong Li Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tong_Li_Comics),<sup>[104]</sup> and in Thailand by [Bongkoch Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongkoch_Comics).<sup>[105][106]</sup>
The President Cat Picture books [\[ edit \]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aria_%28manga%29&action=edit&section=24)

In March 2007, Mag Garden published a series of three Aria [picture books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Picture_book). Each hardcover book contains a full-color short manga story focused on a cat president, and includes an additional collectible item written and illustrated by Amano Kozue.<sup>[207]</sup>

President Hime Picture Book ([ISBN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISBN_%28identifier%29) [978-4-86127-338-4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:BookSources/978-4-86127-338-4)) was published 20 March 2007.<sup>[209]</sup>

President Aria Picture Book ([ISBN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISBN_%28identifier%29) [978-4-86127-339-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:BookSources/978-4-86127-339-1)) was released 30 March 2007.<sup>[210]</sup>
Sheet Music [\[ edit \]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aria_%28manga%29&action=edit&section=25)

Shinko Music published a selection of [sheet music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheet_music) called Aria the Best Selection ([ISBN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISBN_%28identifier%29) [978-4-401-02030-0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:BookSources/978-4-401-02030-0)) in July 2008. It contained the themes from the three anime seasons of Aria.<sup>[211]</sup>
Reception [\[ edit \]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aria_%28manga%29&action=edit&section=26)

In Japan, new volumes of Aria routinely reached the best-seller list for manga,<sup>[6]</sup> and had sold over 3 million copies as of July 2007, representing 11% of all manga volumes ever sold by its publisher to date.<sup>[212]</sup> In 2009, this number increased to 4 million.<sup>[213]</sup>

The English translation of the Aria manga was described by a reviewer at [The Comics Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Comics_Journal) as "quite conceivably the best comics series ever created for elementary-school girls," calling it "a masterpiece of storytelling and illustration, gorgeous to look at and a feast for the young imagination in its ability to present an inviting, fully realized world."<sup>[6]</sup> Aqua and Aria together have been praised for their joyful calm,<sup>[214][215][216]</sup> vividly depicted futuristic world,<sup>[217]</sup> moments of magic,<sup>[216][218]</sup> and sense of whimsy.<sup>[217][218][219]</sup> Amano's artwork is praised for her crisp lines and details, especially in the backgrounds and landscapes.<sup>[219][220]</sup> Amano has also been criticized for confusingly giving every character a name that begins

footnotes.content: Akari and Aika lost inside the Never-ending Waterways (from Aqua volume 1)

blocks.content: with A,<sup>[216][218][221]</sup> for letting some slice-of-life stories "drift too far out,"<sup>[215]</sup> and for making Akari's character too sweet and effusive.<sup>[222]</sup>

In 2006, the anime of Aria was ranked in the top 100 animated television series of all time in a poll by [TV Asahi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TV_Asahi).<sup>[223]</sup> As of June 2007, the first two seasons of the anime adaptation had sold more than 300,000 DVDs.<sup>[212]</sup>

The anime has been praised for its quiet atmosphere,<sup>[224][225][226]</sup> beautiful visuals<sup>[227]</sup>— especially the backgrounds and character designs<sup>[228]</sup>— and exceptional soundtrack.<sup>[229][230]</sup> [Anime News Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anime_News_Network) described the first season as "a gorgeous future fantasy populated with loveable characters", where "each episode is a finely fashioned [tone poem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tone_poem) steeped in a love of the slow rhythms of everyday life and told with an elegant self-possession that places it light-years beyond the vulgar moralizing of most "uplifting" stories."<sup>[224]</sup>[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN) contrasted Aria with [Maria-sama ga Miteru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria-sama_ga_Miteru) as another series where not much happens,

noting that "Maria-sama ratchets up the tension level whenever possible, though, and never mind that all the drama revolves around something completely inconsequential. Aria, on the other hand, is calm and relaxed. It freely admits that the plot is not the point."<sup>[231]</sup> Several reviewers cited the characters as key to the appeal of the series,[226][232][233] though some criticized the characters as unrealistic;<sup>[234]</sup> the voice acting of Erino Hazuki (Akari) and Junko Minagawa (Akira) were particularly praised.<sup>[235][236]</sup> Several reviewers point out that the series does not fit all tastes, being a slow-paced drama with an optimistic outlook.<sup>[237][238][239]</sup>
